patterns.usage_note: Emphatic にして takes an age or an ordinal attempt and presents it as remarkable — startlingly late or early (三十路にして, 五十にして), or hard-won (三度目にして). The startlingly-short-span reading (一夜にして, 一瞬にして) belongs to the sibling instrumental entry. It carries a formal, written flavour and survives in set phrases such as ローマは一日にして成らず; casual speech would use で or たった〜で instead. The same form has two other lives worth recognizing: joining two properties of one person (学者にして詩人), and, chiefly in older or stiff prose, meaning "even" (彼にしてこの失敗) where modern Japanese would say 彼でさえ or 彼ほどの人でも.

examples.ruby: 五十[ごじゅう]にして、父[ちち]は再[ふたた]び大学[だいがく]に通[かよ]い始[はじ]めた。
examples.english: At fifty, my father started going back to university.

examples.ruby: 十六[じゅうろく]にして、隣[となり]の子[こ]は三[さん]か国語[こくご]を操[あやつ]る。
examples.english: At sixteen, the kid next door already handles three languages.

examples.ruby: 三度目[さんどめ]の挑戦[ちょうせん]にして、姉[あね]の短編[たんぺん]が入選[にゅうせん]した。
examples.english: On her third try, and only then, my sister's short story made the cut.
